q1_issues.issue: The reporting frame "is usually considered to be" is dropped entirely and the property is asserted of the kind outright, so the parse states as fact what the text only reports as a general opinion — a violation of "assert only what the text states".
Same flattening on the negated conjunct: "not objective" is asserted at strength 0.0 at top level rather than under the dropped "considered" frame.

q2_gaps: impersonal / agentless reported attitude with a non-finite small-clause complement ("X is considered/regarded/thought TO BE P") — *Propositional attitudes* is explicitly restricted to a FINITE that-clause and needs an Experiencer holder (there is none here), *Perception reports* needs an eventive complement, and the seem/appear epistemic route is stated only for seem/appear, so no rule covers this construction

adverb of quantification over a state ("usually") — it is not a Manner adverb, and Every / TimesPer / QuantifierPhrase all key on countable occasions or a determiner, so there is no form for hedging how generally a reported property holds
notes: The compound decomposition of mental_world (genus + adjectival modifier genus) and the strength-0.0 negation of the second conjunct are both correct in shape, and 1.0/0.9 matches the definite-singular kind precedent ("the dodo is extinct"). Whether "the mental world" is a kind (Inheritance) or a unique individual like "the sun" (Member on a witness) is itself borderline under the definite-description rule.
